# UNESCO North West Highlands Geopark

Stretching over 2,000 square kilometres in the far corner of mainland Scotland, the geopark is a spectacular example of different rock geologies.

## At a glance

- Nature & outdoors:
Home to Lewisian Gneiss, the oldest rock in Europe

- Wildlife:
eagles, seabirds, seals

- Towns & villages:
Achiltibuie, Assynt, Coigach, Durness, Kinlochbervie, Kylesku, Lochinver, Ullapool


Map of Scotland

## What to expect

The North West Highlands Geopark is a place where the story of our planet is written across the landscape. Home to the 3-billion-year-old Lewisian Gneiss, the oldest rock in Europe, this remarkable region reveals some of the earliest evidence of life ever discovered on the continent. Every mountain, cliff and coastline offers a glimpse into Earth's earliest moments.

Beyond its geological features, the Geopark captivates at every turn, where white-sand beaches meet rugged peaks, hidden caves, and vast moorlands, peatlands, and ancient forests. Wildlife thrives here, from soaring eagles and seabirds to seals along the shore. Beneath the surface, caves preserve traces of creatures that roamed these lands thousands of years ago, connecting visitors to a world long vanished.

## Plan your adventure in the North West Highlands Geopark

#### Knockan Crag National Nature Reserve

Visit Knockan Crag National Nature Reserve and its famous Rock Route, explore the Moine Thrust Zone, where groundbreaking geological discoveries changed our understanding of mountain formation, and follow the Geopark's driving and cycling routes to uncover remarkable geological landscapes.

[Follow the North West Highlands Rock Route](https://www.nature.scot/doc/north-west-highlands-rock-route)

#### The Rock Stop

Visit the Rock Stop - the North West Highlands Geopark's visitor centre and an excellent place to begin your journey through the geopark. Located near Unapool (not to be confused with Ullapool!), this centre features exhibits that explain the region's world-famous geology. Visitors can browse books and gifts, pick up maps and local information, and gain a deeper appreciation of the landscapes, wildlife and communities that make the geopark so special.

[Visit the Rock Stop Visitor Centre & Café](https://nwhgeopark.com/exploring/the-rock-stop/)

#### Walking routes in the Geopark

For a more advanced and adventurous day out, you can tackle mountains such as Stac Pollaidh, Suilven, Cul Mòr and Ben More Assynt for spectacular views over lochs, islands, and surrounding peaks. If you're looking for a more gentle wander, enjoy The Old Man of Stoer, the River Inver and Glencanisp circuit, and Achnahaird Bay, or join guided walking, scrambling or mountaineering adventures with local experts.

[Discover walking routes around Ullapool & Assynt](https://www.walkhighlands.co.uk/ullapool/)

#### The Assynt and Coigach Creative Trail

Experience the Assynt and Coigach Creative Trail, visit artists' studios, galleries and craft workshops and browse the Balnakeil Craft Village, home to local artisans and food producers.

[Explore the Assynt & Coigach Creative Trail](https://www.coigach-assynt.org/2019/07/assynt-coigach-creative-trail/)

### Rock Route

This is a route between a series of information boards telling you more about the local landscape and set throughout the geopark. There are 14 boards to find, each accompanied by an audio guide. They'll help you trace the marks left over the years by mountains, glaciers and sea level changes right across this incredible area.

[Follow the Rock Route](https://nwhgeopark.com/the-rock-route/)

## Towns and villages within the North West Highlands Geopark

Adventure across the iconic bridge in Kylesku, feel the sand beneath your feet on Kinlochbervie's golden shores, or look up at the imposing peaks in Assynt. Here are some welcoming places you can choose as your base to explore everything the geopark has to offer.

previousnext

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2026/10/01/summer-isles)

### [Achiltibuie](https://visitcoigach.com/more-about-achiltibuie/)

Overlooking the Summer Isles and open sea, Achiltibuie is set in magnificent mountain and coastal scenery on the remote north west coast.

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2026/05/01/ardvreck-castle-on-loch-assynt)

### [Assynt](https://www.discoverassynt.co.uk/)

Often regarded as the heart of the Geopark, it is famed for its isolated mountains as well as its geological significance, lochs, and ancient castles.

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2023/06/21/loch-na-gainmhich.jpg)

### [Coigach](https://visitcoigach.com/)

Coigach offers dramatic coastal scenery, hidden beaches, island views, and a thriving creative community.

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2023/05/31/durness)

### [Durness](https://discoverhighlandsandislands.scot/en/visitor/location/durness)

Renowned for its white-sand beaches and dramatic cliffs, Durness is a thriving village surrounded by the dramatic landscape of Sutherland.

previousnext

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2024/04/17/oldshoremore-bay)

### [Kinlochbervie](https://www.kinlochbervie.info/)

Surrounded by spectacular cliffs, sandy coves, and wild landscapes, it is an ideal base for exploring the Geopark's far north-west.

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2025/09/04/kylesku-bridge.jpg)

### [Kylesku](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/kylesku/kylesku/index.html)

Nestled beside the dramatic Kylesku Bridge, it is a picturesque stopping point and gateway to nearby waterfalls, wildlife, and mountain scenery.

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2023/01/17/loch-assynt)

### [Lochinver](https://discoverhighlandsandislands.scot/en/visitor/location/lochinver)

Lochinver is known for fresh seafood, access to iconic mountains and stunning views across sea lochs and rugged landscapes.

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2022/06/24/ullapool-boats-harbour)

### [Ullapool](https://www.ullapool.com/)

Visit the picturesque fishing town of Ullapool.

## Scotland’s UNESCO Trail

The first country in the world to bring together 16 UNESCO sites into one trail. Are you read to discover the wonders of Scotland?

[Explore the UNESCO trail](https://www.visitscotland.com/places-to-go/unesco)

## Plan your trip to the North West Highlands Geopark

- Getting there
- Accessibility

### Getting there

Bus and coach

## Bus and coach

Inverness serves as the Highlands’ main transport hub, with regular rail services from Edinburgh, Glasgow, and other Scottish & UK cities, as well as domestic and international flights.

From Inverness, you can travel onwards to key geopark communities including [Ullapool](https://www.citylink.co.uk/our-routes-and-timetables/inverness-ullapool/) and [Durness](https://www.thedurnessbus.com/805-inverness/) by bus in about 3 hours.

[Plan your journey by train in Scotland](https://www.visitscotland.com/travel-planning/railway)

[Travel through Scotland by bus](https://www.visitscotland.com/travel-planning/bus-coach)

* * *

Driving

## Driving

The easiest and most flexible way to reach the geopark is by car.

From Inverness, the A835 leads to Ullapool, while the A837 and A894 continue north through the heart of the Geopark. You can also explore the area as part of a trip along the famous North Coast 500 route.

[Have a look at the leaflet on touring the North West Highlands Geopark \| PDF 12.7MB](https://www.nwhgeopark.com/wp-content/uploads/Tour-Guide-Leaflet.pdf)

* * *

### Accessibility

The North West Highlands Geopark is making its remarkable landscapes and geological heritage more accessible, but accessibility can vary significantly depending on where you visit. While some attractions, visitor facilities and viewpoints are suitable for visitors with limited mobility, much of the geopark's appeal lies in its rugged mountains, remote beaches, and natural terrain, which can present challenges.

### [The Scottish Highlands](https://www.visitscotland.com/places-to-go/highlands)

Green valleys, vibrant culture, towering mountains, historic castles and peaceful lochs: the Highlands is the Scotland of your imagination.

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2022/12/07/inverness-cathedral)

### [Inverness](https://www.visitscotland.com/places-to-go/inverness)

Discover Inverness, our capital of the Highlands, with scenic riverside walks, historic sights and a warm local atmosphere.

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2026/09/30/dingieshowe)

### [Orkney](https://www.visitscotland.com/places-to-go/islands/orkney)

These astonishing islands shelter Scotland’s ancient past, from standing stones to entire early settlements carved into the coastline.

## FAQs

What is a geopark?

### What is a geopark?

A geopark, or UNESCO Global Geopark, is an area of outstanding geological and scientific importance. These special places are protected and monitored to help us better understand the geophysical and climate forces that shape our planet. Scotland now has three Global Geoparks. Each of these ancient landscapes gives a chance to learn more about geology, sustainability, and conservation.

[More info on UNESCO Global Geoparks in Scotland](https://unesco.org.uk/our-network/geoparks)

* * *

When is the best time to visit North West Highlands Geopark?

### When is the best time to visit North West Highlands Geopark?

The North West Highlands Geopark is a year-round destination. Between May and September, longer days and milder weather provide ideal conditions for exploring. Spring and autumn offer fewer crowds and stunning seasonal colours, while winter rewards adventurous travellers with dramatic landscapes, dark skies, and the possibility of seeing the Northern Lights.

* * *

Where can I stay in the North West Highlands Geopark?

### Where can I stay in the North West Highlands Geopark?

Whether you would like to stay on a working farm, in a rustic shepherd’s hut, a welcoming B&B or a luxury cottage with a hot tub, you can find plenty of options for your biosphere stay.

The North West Highlands Geopark offers a wide range of accommodation, from cosy guesthouses and boutique hotels to self-catering cottages, campsites, and luxury lodges. Whether you're looking for a base for hiking adventures, a coastal escape, or a remote retreat beneath dark Highland skies, you'll find many different options across the geopark's communities.

[Find your hostel stay in the North West Highlands Geopark](https://www.hostellingscotland.org.uk/inspiration/discover-scotlands-nw-highlands/)

[Stay in a hotel in the North West Highlands Geopark](https://www.tripadvisor.co.uk/HotelsNear-g635690-d8004886-North_West_Highlands_Geopark-Lairg_Caithness_and_Sutherland_Scottish_Highlands_Scotland.html)

[Find accommodation in the Ullapool area](https://www.ullapool.com/where-to-stay/)

* * *

How long should I stay in the North West Highlands Geopark?

### How long should I stay in the North West Highlands Geopark?

While it's possible to experience some of the North West Highlands Geopark's highlights in a day or two, you can easily spend a week or more exploring the vast richness and diversity of mountains, coastlines, beaches, and geological wonders within the different areas of the geopark.

* * *

## Being a responsible traveller

It is important to explore Scotland's UNESCO Trail in a sustainable and responsible way. Stay in accredited places to stay, shop local, or take public transport where you can.

[Find out more about being sustainable in Scotland](https://www.visitscotland.com/planning/responsible-tourism)
